brief: Drives real concurrent load at a server with separate processes and measures the response time clients see, to show the knee of the curve.
detail: The knee, response time exploding as throughput nears its ceiling, is the signature of queueing, and queueing needs concurrent arrivals that a serial in-process harness can never produce. The driver spawns a target stzAppServer as a child, or aims at a server already running, then runs a number of driver processes at once, each firing its requests one after another and printing every duration it observed, wait in the accept queue included. It is a closed-loop model: a driver fires its next request when the previous answers. DriveWith gives one level, Curve several, Explain narrates the knee. Spawning processes was not run for this reference; the settings, AimAt, WaitReady against a closed port and Explain were.
receiver:
o1 = new stzLoadDriver()
o1.SetBusyMs(5)
o1.SetRequestsPerDriver(10)
o1.AimAt("127.0.0.1", 1)
example: #--> Driven load -- target 127.0.0.1:1, D ~5ms CPU/request, 0 level(s).
